title: Geometric preservation for compatible open quotient models
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an open immersion $j:U\to X$ of Noetherian schemes, with $\ell$ invertible in their global sections. Use completed integral coefficients and positive quotient rings $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $C$ be any compatible open tensor context [lem-pur-completed-open-tensor-representatives]: it contains the actual normalized open operations, coefficient comparisons, coherent derived-system calculi and compatible ordinary reduction presentations. With these same operations, finite extension is naturally isomorphic to intrinsic finite-coefficient extension by zero at each $A_n$. Integral extension and restriction preserve $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$, and preserve every supplied common cohomological interval of quotient reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Precisely, FiniteExtensionModel and IntegralGeometry of [def-sf-open-tensor-quotient-data] hold for $C.operations$. No tensor augmentation, tensor-completion chain presentation, or strict tensor square is asserted.

proof.text: Use the unique section-normalized finite restriction presentation of the supplied Operations. Its left-adjoint comparison gives the required finite extension model. For restriction compose that presentation with uniqueness of the right adjoint of intrinsic extension by zero and the unit-preserving tensor/intrinsic pullback coordinate isomorphism. All coefficient rings have positive exponent n+1 and hence are finite.

Translate intrinsic derived completeness to IntegralOpenReduction.complete using the legacy completeness comparison; an auxiliary prime different from l supplies its irrelevant finite-field datum. The compatible context supplies completeness of both outputs and natural reduction isomorphisms r and s. Compose them with reductionEvaluation, the derived square of extensionEvaluation (respectively the restriction-evaluation square built from the equivalence unit and counit), and the finite model comparisons. Thus each quotient of the output is isomorphic to the exact finite operation on the input quotient.

For extension apply the finite open constructibility and interval theorem to each quotient. For restriction use the proved pullback_constructible and constructible_of_iso helpers in FiniteImmersionConstructibilityInterval: the actual fibre-product partition pulls back the locally constant finite-stalk strata, via CartesianStratumModuleRestriction. Exact pullback commutes with homology and sends zero to zero, so output cohomological support is contained in input support. Transport finite constructibility and the support interval across the quotient isomorphisms. Completeness plus one common interval gives integral constructibility; repeat the same calculation for every separately supplied common interval.
